text:
Predicates:
TakeTest(x) ::: x takes the GRE test.
Cost(x, 205) ::: x costs US $205.
ProvideFinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
Prove(x, y) ::: y proves x.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x has economic hardship.
Difficulty(x) ::: x has difficulty.
Money(x) ::: x has too little money.
Resources(x) ::: x has too few resources.
LiveIn(x, y) ::: x lives in y.
OutOfWork(x, y) ::: x has been out of work for more than y.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
Premises:
Cost(TakeTest(gre), 205) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x (TakeTest(x) ∧ Prove(EconomicHardship, x) → ProvideFinancialAid(ETS, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (EconomicHardship(x) ↔ (Difficulty(x) ∧ (Money(x) ∨ Resources(x)))) ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
LiveIn(Tom, SingleParentFamily) ∧ OutOfWork(dad, year) ∧ (year > 1) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family. His dad has been out of work for more than a year.
Conclusion:
∃x (TakeTest(gre) ∧ Prove(EconomicHardship, x) ∧ x = Tom) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
